enumeration.method: Independent small-cap formal and bold overview heading enumeration, with visual comparison of all nine complete labeled statements.

checks: Six formal Theorems and three bold labeled overview statements are preserved separately: nine source occurrences, six distinct printed theorem numbers. Heading enumeration excludes citations, Table 1 and proofs. Main text ends with the Discussion on page 25; supplementary and appendix bodies are excluded.

Twenty-three entries and twelve supporting passages preserve Holder and Besov conventions, latent pushforwards, IPMs, GAN estimator, both model assumptions, separate manifold/density regularity, errors and coverings, wavelet formulas and all specified neural classes.

Independent reconstruction gives 57 direct uses and 86 related connections. Existential overview classes and arbitrary classes in Theorem 3.1 do not acquire later network prerequisites. Interpolation Theorem 5.1 has no GAN/network dependencies. Uniform and candidate-specific discrimination errors remain distinct.

The overview of 5.1 imposes density regularity on both maps; its formal statement imposes it only on g-star. Theorem 5.8 overview has gamma up to beta+1, while the formal statement prints tilde-beta+1. Subsequent broader-range prose is retained separately. Theorem 5.4 preserves its untilded critical indicator.

Exact hat-wavelet implementations and the chi-numerical regularity formula live in appendices. Only the main-text descriptions, bounds, formulas and references are retained. The census does not substitute manifold regularity for the numerical condition or claim a fully specified executable neural construction.

Fourteen source scope/convention issues remain explicit, including the d=1 zero denominator, delta=0 logarithms, network coefficient/index mismatches, scaling-wavelet name reversal, Holder/Besov endpoints and exact optimizer selections. Original statements are not corrected or certified as proofs.

Every entry has literal source terms, faithful model/definition/source-passage labels and source-matching selectors. All 86 theorem connections have explicit same-paper definition paths and explanations. Shared terminology does not merge distinct error or network definitions.

The six content JSON artifacts reproduce byte for byte from the retained per-paper scripts. Independent heading enumeration, source-specific formula checks, graph reconstruction, frozen artifact hashes and schema validation protect the reviewed extraction.

source_notes.description: The overview of Theorem 5.1 imposes both regularity conditions on both maps. The formal Theorem 5.1 imposes manifold regularity on both but density regularity only on g-star. Preserve the two labeled statements separately.

Theorem 5.8 overview asserts simultaneous gamma in [1,beta+1]; the formal theorem prints [1,tilde-beta+1]. Subsequent prose extends the claimed conclusion when beta+1>=d/2. All versions retain their original ranges without merging.

Theorems 3.1 and 5.4 minimize over delta in [0,1] while using log(delta^{-1}) and possibly nonpositive powers. No endpoint convention is supplied. Theorem 5.4 also prints beta+1=d/2 in its indicator although its other terms use tilde-beta; do not silently replace it.

Global d includes 1. With tilde-beta+1=min(beta+1,d/2), the resolution denominator 2 tilde-beta+d equals zero at d=1, and [1,tilde-beta+1] is empty. No lower dimension restriction repairing these formulas is added by the census.

The GAN, optimal discriminators and Besov approximation use exact argmin/argmax without specifying measurable selection. The covering definition uses argmin as a selected cover and does not state centers must lie in F. Preserve these conventions rather than invent a selection algorithm or altered covering definition.

Page 12 initially calls psi the scaling function and phi the wavelet, while page 13 periodization and page 14 call phi the scaling function. The Euclidean l range ends at 2^p-1, but periodic/network sums end at 2^d or 2^p. Preserve the printed roles and ranges without correcting the basis.

Formula (3.11) sums over z but prints coefficient alpha(j,l,w)_i, with its bound using z. Network sums do not explicitly supply the separate constant/coarse mode used in the source bases. Logarithmic and spatial summation endpoints have no explicit rounding convention. These details remain unresolved rather than repaired.

The hat-wavelet constructions refer to (A.4), (A.5) and (A.10) and Lemmas A.1-A.2. Preserve main-text precision, coefficient and architecture formulas, but do not claim that the appendix-only neural implementation has been extracted.

The chi-numerical regularity condition in (5.1) is defined in Appendix E.1. Main text gives only a description and a claimed implication to manifold regularity. Its exact formula and admissible chi are unresolved within the permitted main-text scope.

The Hölder display places max_i before the first derivative sum and leaves the second unparenthesized. Its definition starts at eta>0, while the pushforward display invokes H^0 test functions. The finite-q Besov norm is later used at infinity and on periodic/vector spaces without all modifications written out. Preserve these conventions explicitly.

The GAN display places the summation directly before D(X_i)-D(g(U_i)) without enclosing parentheses. The accompanying empirical-loss explanation indicates paired sample terms; the original display is retained rather than silently inserting grouping into its quotation.
Formula (4.2) prints D(g(U))-D(g-prime(u)) inside its expectation, mixing uppercase U and lowercase u. Preserve this original typo separately from its apparent intended meaning.

The generic GAN definition requires Holder-bounded classes; the instantiated classes are expressed by approximate wavelet coefficients, with no explicit Holder-ball intersection in (4.1),(4.3),(5.1). Do not invent this intersection or infer exact Holder membership solely from approximation/Besov membership.

The class construction initially states eta in (0,beta+1) and delta in (0,1), then uses eta=beta+1. Global n>=1 also permits log(n)=0 and delta=1 in displayed rates/classes. The census preserves these source endpoints and does not add an unprinted sufficiently-large-n clause.

ambient_resolution.T5.1-overview: D1,D2,D4 define the maps, pushforwards and distances. Both g and g-star satisfy D8 and D9 in this overview. Epsilon, gamma, constants and the closeness threshold are bound here. No GAN estimator or neural network enters this deterministic inequality.

Delta_G and Delta_D are distinct errors D11-D12, and D13 the two class-covering numbers. Delta, n and constants are locally bound with A1-A4 conventions. ambient_resolution.T4.1: D1,D2,D4,D5 define the generic objects, while D17-D18 specify exactly G and D in (4.1)-(4.2), including the wavelet precision, 1/n-cover and selected optimal discriminators. All network prerequisites follow those class definitions; the overview does not replace this full statement. No manifold assumption or proof regularization operator is added.
ambient_resolution.T5.1: D1,D2,D4,D8,D9 resolve this deterministic interpolation inequality. Manifold regularity is imposed on both maps but density regularity only on g-star, unlike the overview. No compatible map from the appendix, GAN class or stochastic estimator is required to state the result.
ambient_resolution.T5.4: D1,D2,D4,D5,D8,D9 resolve the target and estimator. G,D are D19,D21 with the cap and resolution (5.2), and unresolved numerical regularity in G. Delta_G is D11 at the current tilde-beta+1 regularity. D22 gives the supremum of fixed-generator composition covering numbers using D13. D23 gives the candidate-specific Besov discrepancy whose expectation is evaluated at ghat. The printed untilded critical indicator and delta=0 endpoint are retained.
ambient_resolution.T5.7: D1,D2,D4,D5,D8,D9 define the target regularity, distributions, IPM and GAN; D19,D21 fix the numerical-condition generator and capped discriminator. The rate has tilde-beta in numerator and denominator and no printed max with n^{-1/2}; do not change it. Proof error terms and compatibility are not statement dependencies.
ambient_resolution.T5.8: The target regularity and GAN are D1,D2,D4,D5,D8,D9, with actual G,D from D19,D21. The statement prints gamma in [1,tilde-beta+1] but beta in the final rate. Overview and subsequent extended-range explanation remain separate. The closeness hypothesis of the proof interpolation theorem is not an extra assumption here.
